days.title: Culture: la escuela
days.work: Read about school in Mexico or Chile (uniforms, recreo, schedules) and list four differences from your homeschool day.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer schedule questions in a short interview and take a numbers-to-100 dictation.

days.title: -ar endings
days.work: Learn infinitive, stem, and endings (-o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an) and conjugate hablar and estudiar in a chart.

days.title: Drill
days.work: Complete Conjuguemos -ar verb practice until you score 90%, then write 10 original sentences.

days.title: Who does what?
days.work: Describe what each family member does on a weekday using -ar verbs and time expressions.

days.title: Questions
days.work: Form yes/no and question-word questions (¿Qué estudias? ¿Cuándo trabajas?) and interview a parent.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an -ar verb conjugation and sentence-writing quiz.

days.title: Review: units 1–2
days.work: Review greetings, numbers, dates, time, and weather with a self-made flashcard set and a practice listening quiz.

days.title: Review: units 3–5
days.work: Review ser, adjectives, gustar, classroom vocabulary, and -ar verbs with a practice test.

days.title: Speaking exam
days.work: Do a 3-minute interpersonal interview with a parent covering name, origin, personality, likes, and schedule.

days.title: Written exam
days.work: Take the semester written exam (listening, reading, grammar, and a 10-sentence writing prompt).

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Fill in a can-do checklist for semester 1 and set two goals for semester 2.

weeks.topic: El desayuno y el almuerzo: food vocabulary
objectives: Say what you eat and drink

days.title: Breakfast foods
days.work: Learn 12 breakfast foods and drinks and label a picture of your own breakfast.

days.title: Lunch foods
days.work: Learn 12 lunch foods and drinks and sort all foods into a category chart (frutas, verduras, carnes, bebidas).

days.title: Me encanta / me gustan
days.work: Learn me gusta(n) and me encanta(n) with plural nouns and write 10 sentences about foods.

days.title: Encuesta
days.work: Ask three family members ¿Qué comes en el desayuno? and summarize the answers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a food vocabulary and gustar/encantar quiz.

objectives: Talk about eating and drinking habits

days.title: -er verbs
days.work: Learn the -er endings and conjugate comer, beber, and leer in a chart.

days.title: -ir verbs
days.work: Learn the -ir endings, noting nosotros -imos, and conjugate vivir, escribir, compartir.

days.title: Drill
days.work: Complete Conjuguemos -er/-ir practice to 90%, then write 10 sentences with frequency words (siempre, a veces, nunca).

days.title: Interview
days.work: Interview a parent about their eating habits with eight questions using -er/-ir verbs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an -ar/-er/-ir conjugation quiz.

weeks.topic: Para mantener la salud: healthy eating and plural adjectives
objectives: Use plural adjectives and ser with foods

days.title: Comida sana
days.work: Learn 12 vegetable and protein words and classify foods as bueno/malo para la salud.

days.title: Plural adjectives
days.work: Describe 10 foods with ser and agreeing adjectives: Las zanahorias son sabrosas.

days.title: Nutrition labels
days.work: Read a Spanish nutrition label (información nutricional) and answer questions about grasa, azúcar, and calorías.

days.title: Mi plato
days.work: Draw a balanced plate and write a 6-sentence description of a healthy lunch, using para mantener la salud debes...

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a reading quiz on a short healthy-eating article and present your plate orally.

objectives: Identify traditional foods of several countries

days.title: Regional foods
days.work: Research one traditional dish each from Mexico, Spain, Venezuela, and Peru and add photos and captions to your map.

days.title: Tortilla: two meanings
days.work: Compare the Mexican corn tortilla and the Spanish tortilla española; write five comparison sentences.

days.title: El mercado
days.work: Watch a video of a Latin American market and list 10 foods you recognize in Spanish.

days.title: Cocina
days.work: Prepare a simple recipe (guacamole or tortilla española) with a parent, narrating each step in Spanish.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a short reflection comparing a family meal tradition with one you studied.

materials: paper or slides for a menu

days.title: Menu design
days.work: Design a bilingual café menu with 12 items and prices in pesos or euros.

days.title: Descriptions
days.work: Write a one-sentence Spanish description for each menu item using adjectives.

days.title: Ordering chunks
days.work: Learn the chunks ¿Qué quieres comer? and Quisiera... and practice ordering from your menu.

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Run a café role-play with a family member as customer, using numbers for prices.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Take the unit 6 test: food listening, -er/-ir verbs, and a short writing on your eating habits.

weeks.assessment: Menu project rubric and unit 6 test.

days.title: Family words
days.work: Learn 20 family words and label a photo collage of your family.

days.title: Relationships
days.work: Read a family tree of a fictional Spanish-speaking family and answer 10 ¿Quién es...? questions.

days.title: Describing family
days.work: Write six sentences describing family members' personalities and appearance with ser.

days.title: Mascotas
days.work: Add pets and describe them; share a short video tour of family photos in Spanish.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a family vocabulary quiz.

weeks.topic: The verb tener and possessive adjectives

days.title: Tener
days.work: Learn the forms of tener (tengo, tienes...) and complete a Conjuguemos tener drill.

days.title: Ages
days.work: Ask and answer ¿Cuántos años tiene...? for 10 family members and friends.

days.title: Possessives
days.work: Learn mi/tu/su/nuestro/vuestro and their plurals and complete a 20-item practice.

days.title: Conversation
days.work: Discuss your family with a parent: how many siblings, cousins, and pets, and who is older or younger.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a tener and possessives quiz.

days.title: Expressions
days.work: Learn tener hambre, sed, frío, calor, sueño, miedo, prisa, razón and caption 10 pictures.

days.title: Tener que
days.work: Write a to-do list using tener que + infinitive for each family member this week.

days.title: Celebrations
days.work: Read about the quinceañera and the cumpleaños tradition of las mañanitas; listen to Las mañanitas and write down five words you hear.

days.title: Mi fiesta
days.work: Describe your last family party in present-tense sentences: who is there, what they eat, what they have.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a tener expressions quiz with a listening section.

days.title: Apellidos
days.work: Learn how Spanish double surnames (apellido paterno y materno) work and write your name in that format.

days.title: Build the tree
days.work: Create a family tree poster with at least 12 relatives, labels, and ages.

days.title: Script
days.work: Write a 10–12 sentence presentation of your family using tener, ser, possessives, and gustar.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Practice presenting with notes on index cards (key words only) and record a practice run.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Present the family tree (2 minutes) and take the unit 7 written test.

weeks.assessment: Family tree presentation rubric and unit test.

days.title: Estar
days.work: Learn estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están and when to use estar for location and feelings.

days.title: Prepositions
days.work: Place a stuffed animal in 12 locations and describe each: El gato está debajo de la mesa.

days.title: Where is it?
days.work: Hide five objects and give a parent Spanish clues to find them; then switch roles.

days.title: Ser vs. estar intro
days.work: Sort 15 sentences into ser (origin, description) or estar (location, feelings) and explain each choice.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an estar and prepositions quiz.

objectives: Ask and say where places are

days.title: Places
days.work: Learn 16 places in a town and label a hand-drawn map of your neighborhood.

days.title: Map questions
days.work: Answer ¿Dónde está la biblioteca? questions using prepositions on your map.

days.title: La plaza
days.work: Read about the central plaza in Spanish and Latin American towns and compare it with a California downtown.

days.title: Virtual tour
days.work: Use Google Maps Street View to tour a plaza in Oaxaca or Salamanca and write 8 sentences about what is there.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a places vocabulary quiz with a map-reading section.

weeks.topic: ¿Adónde vas? The verb ir and question words
objectives: Say where people go and when

days.title: Ir
days.work: Learn voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van and the contraction a + el = al.

days.title: Question words
days.work: Review ¿Qué? ¿Quién? ¿Dónde? ¿Adónde? ¿Cuándo? ¿Con quién? ¿Por qué? and write 10 questions about weekend plans.

days.title: My week
days.work: Fill a planner with where you go each day and write 7 sentences with ir and time expressions.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Interview a family member about where they go during the week and write a short report.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an ir and question words quiz.

objectives: Read a city map in Spanish

days.title: Direction words
days.work: Learn derecha, izquierda, todo derecho, cuadra, esquina and follow parent's spoken directions around the house.

days.title: Map practice
days.work: Trace routes on a printed map of a Spanish city center as you listen to recorded directions.

days.title: Giving directions
days.work: Write directions from your house to three local places using memorized chunks (dobla a la derecha, sigue derecho).

days.title: Info gap
days.work: Play an information-gap map game with a parent: each has half the places and must ask ¿Dónde está...?

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a listening quiz following directions on a map.

objectives: Create a guided tour of your town

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose five places in your town and write two sentences about each: where it is and what people do there.

days.title: Record
days.work: Film or photograph the places and record a narrated tour in Spanish (2 minutes).

days.title: Reading
days.work: Read a short tourist brochure about a Spanish-speaking city and answer comprehension questions.

days.title: Conversation
days.work: Role-play a tourist asking a local for directions to three places.

days.title: Unit 8 test
days.work: Take the unit 8 test on estar, ir, places, and directions.

weeks.assessment: Town tour video rubric and unit test.

weeks.topic: Los deportes e ir a + infinitive
objectives: Talk about future plans with ir a + infinitive

days.title: Sports
days.work: Learn 12 sports and jugar a and describe which sports family members play.

days.title: Ir a + infinitive
days.work: Learn voy a jugar, vas a ver... and write 10 sentences about plans for next weekend.

days.title: Culture: fútbol
days.work: Read about a famous soccer rivalry (Real Madrid–Barcelona or Boca–River) and summarize it in five Spanish sentences.

days.title: Plans calendar
days.work: Make a two-week plans calendar and tell a parent your plans using time expressions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an ir a + infinitive quiz.

days.title: Invitation chunks
days.work: Learn ¿Quieres ir...?, ¡Claro que sí!, Lo siento, no puedo, tengo que... and practice in pairs.

days.title: Texting
days.work: Write a Spanish text-message exchange inviting a friend to a game, including time and place.

days.title: Phone call
days.work: Make a simulated phone call to invite a family member to an event and respond to their excuse.

days.title: Cultural norms
days.work: Read about punctuality and social plans in Latin America and Spain and discuss differences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Hold a recorded unscripted invitation conversation.

days.title: Review: units 1–5
days.work: Review greetings, calendar, ser, gustar, school, and -ar verbs with a practice test.

days.title: Review: units 6–9
days.work: Review food, -er/-ir verbs, family, tener, estar, ir, and ir a + infinitive with Conjuguemos drills.

days.title: Reading practice
days.work: Read three short Spanish texts (menu, family profile, town brochure) and answer questions.

days.title: Speaking practice
days.work: Do a mock 3-minute interview covering all topics of the year.

days.title: Writing practice
days.work: Write a practice paragraph about yourself, your family, and your weekend plans.

objectives: Demonstrate Novice Mid proficiency in all three modes

days.title: Interpretive
days.work: Read an authentic text (a pen-pal profile or town website) and listen to a short audio, answering comprehension questions.

days.title: Interpersonal
days.work: Hold a 4-minute conversation with a parent about yourself, family, school, food, and plans.

days.title: Presentational
days.work: Write and present 'Mi vida' (12–15 sentences) covering all 1A topics.

days.title: Cultures
days.work: Present one cultural comparison from the year (food, greetings, plazas, or celebrations).

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Complete a can-do self-assessment and set goals for Spanish 1B.

weeks.assessment: Integrated performance assessment rubric (interpretive, interpersonal, presentational).

courses.subject: VAPA
courses.title: Visual & Performing Arts 7
courses.description: A rotating arts course covering visual art (drawing, color, printmaking, sculpture), music (notation, listening, ukulele or keyboard performance, composition), theatre (improvisation, scene work, a short play) and media arts (photography and stop-motion animation). Projects connect to the medieval and early-modern cultures studied in history, and students keep a sketchbook/process journal and finish with a family exhibition and performance.
courses.framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools (Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, Media Arts); 2020 CA Arts Framework

standards.VA:Cr1.1.7: Apply methods to overcome creative blocks.
standards.VA:Cr1.2.7: Develop criteria to guide making a work of art or design to meet an identified goal.
standards.VA:Cr2.1.7: Demonstrate persistence in developing skills with various materials, methods and approaches in creating works of art or design.
standards.VA:Cr2.2.7: Demonstrate awareness of ethical responsibility to oneself and others when posting and sharing content online.
standards.VA:Cr2.3.7: Apply visual organizational strategies to design and produce a work of art, design or media that clearly communicates information or ideas.
standards.VA:Cr3.1.7: Reflect on and explain important information about personal artwork in an artist statement or another format.
standards.VA:Pr4.1.7: Compare and contrast how technologies have changed the way artwork is preserved, presented and experienced.
standards.VA:Pr5.1.7: Based on criteria, analyze and evaluate methods for preparing and presenting art.
standards.VA:Pr6.1.7: Compare and contrast viewing and experiencing collections and exhibitions in different venues.
standards.VA:Re7.1.7: Explain how the method of display, the location and the experience of an artwork influence how it is perceived and valued.
standards.VA:Re7.2.7: Analyze multiple ways that images influence specific audiences.
standards.VA:Re8.1.7: Interpret art by analyzing art-making approaches, the characteristics of form and structure, relevant contextual information, subject matter and use of media to identify ideas and mood conveyed.
standards.VA:Re9.1.7: Compare and explain the difference between an evaluation of an artwork based on personal criteria and one based on a set of established criteria.
standards.VA:Cn10.1.7: Individually or collaboratively create art that reflects ideas and values from various cultures or time periods.
standards.VA:Cn11.1.7: Analyze how response to art is influenced by understanding the time and place in which it was created.
standards.MU:Cr1.1.7: Generate rhythmic, melodic and harmonic phrases and variations over harmonic accompaniments within expanded forms.
standards.MU:Cr2.1.7: Select, organize and document personal musical ideas for arrangements, songs and compositions within expanded forms.
standards.MU:Cr3.1.7: Evaluate their own work, applying selected criteria such as appropriate application of elements of music, including style, form and use of sound sources.
standards.MU:Cr3.2.7: Present the final version of their documented personal composition, song or arrangement, demonstrating unity and variety.
standards.MU:Pr4.2.7: When analyzing selected music, read and identify by name or function standard symbols for rhythm, pitch, articulation, dynamics, tempo and form.
standards.MU:Pr4.3.7: Perform contrasting pieces of music, demonstrating as well as explaining how the music's intent is conveyed by interpretation of the elements of music.
standards.MU:Pr5.1.7: Identify and apply collaboratively developed criteria to rehearse, refine and determine when a piece is ready to perform.
standards.MU:Pr6.1.7: Perform music with technical accuracy and stylistic expression to convey the creator's intent.
standards.MU:Re7.2.7: Classify and explain how the elements of music and expressive qualities relate to the structure of contrasting pieces.
standards.MU:Re8.1.7: Describe a personal interpretation of contrasting works and explain how creators' and performers' application of the elements of music convey expressive intent.
standards.MU:Re9.1.7: Select from teacher-provided criteria to evaluate musical works or performances.
standards.MU:Cn11.0.7: Demonstrate understanding of relationships between music and the other arts, other disciplines, varied contexts and daily life.
standards.TH:Cr1.1.7: Investigate multiple perspectives and solutions to staging problems in a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cr2.1.7: Examine and justify original ideas and artistic choices in a drama/theatre work based on critical analysis, background knowledge and historical and cultural context.
standards.TH:Cr3.1.7: Demonstrate focus and concentration in the rehearsal process to analyze and refine choices in a devised or scripted drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Pr4.1.7: Consider multiple planned technical elements during the rehearsal process for a devised or scripted drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Pr5.1.7: Participate in a variety of acting exercises and techniques that can be applied in a rehearsal or drama/theatre performance.
standards.TH:Pr6.1.7: Participate in rehearsals for a drama/theatre work that will be shared with an audience.
standards.TH:Re7.1.7: Compare recurring patterns in drama/theatre works.
standards.TH:Re8.1.7: Identify the artistic choices made in a drama/theatre work through participation and observation.
standards.TH:Re9.1.7: Explain preferences, using supporting evidence and criteria, to evaluate drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cn11.2.7: Research and discuss how a playwright might have intended a drama/theatre work to be produced.
standards.MA:Cr1.1.7: Generate ideas, goals and solutions for original media artworks through application of chosen generative methods.
standards.MA:Cr2.1.7: Design, propose and evaluate artistic ideas, plans, prototypes and production processes for media arts productions.
standards.MA:Cr3.1.7: Coordinate production processes to integrate content and stylistic conventions for determined purpose and meaning in media arts productions.
standards.MA:Pr5.1.7: Exhibit an increasing set of artistic, design, technical and soft skills through performing various roles in producing media artworks.
standards.MA:Pr6.1.7: Evaluate various presentation formats in order to fulfill various tasks and defined processes in the presentation and distribution of media artworks.
standards.MA:Re7.1.7: Describe, compare and analyze the qualities of and relationships between the components and style in media artworks.
standards.MA:Cn10.1.7: Access, evaluate and integrate personal and external resources to inform the creation of original media artworks.

days.title: Sketchbook setup
days.work: Design a sketchbook cover and fill one page with 20 different kinds of lines.

days.title: Blind contour
days.work: Draw your non-dominant hand in blind contour three times for 3 minutes each.

days.title: Modified contour
days.work: Draw a shoe in modified contour, glancing at the paper only at corners.

days.title: Beating creative block
days.work: Try three idea-starters (random object, word prompt, 'draw it 5 ways') and fill a page.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Choose your best contour drawing and write three sentences about line quality.

days.title: Value scale
days.work: Create a 9-step value scale with pencil and a second using hatching and cross-hatching.

days.title: Shading spheres
days.work: Draw and shade three spheres with highlight, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow.

days.title: Egg study
days.work: Light an egg with a lamp and draw it realistically for 25 minutes.

days.title: Texture shading
days.work: Shade a crumpled paper bag using varied pencil grades.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare your egg study to a Renaissance drawing and note one technique to improve.

weeks.assessment: Value scale and shaded egg study.

objectives: Draw in one- and two-point perspective
materials: print of Raphael's School of Athens

days.title: One-point
days.work: Draw block letters of your initials in one-point perspective.

days.title: Finding vanishing points
days.work: Find and trace orthogonals in The School of Athens to locate its vanishing point.

days.title: One-point room
days.work: Draw your bedroom or a hallway in one-point perspective.

days.title: Two-point
days.work: Draw a street corner of buildings in two-point perspective.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Explain in writing how perspective changed art in the Renaissance.

days.title: Face proportions
days.work: Learn standard face proportions and draw a guideline face.

days.title: Features
days.work: Practice drawing eyes, nose and mouth from a mirror, one page each.

days.title: Self-portrait sketch
days.work: Sketch a self-portrait from a mirror using guidelines.

days.title: Self-portrait shading
days.work: Add value to the self-portrait using the light source.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare the self-portrait to an early-year sketch and list improvements.

weeks.topic: Still life composition and artist statement
objectives: Compose and render a still life

days.title: Arranging
days.work: Arrange 4–5 objects and use a paper viewfinder to make three thumbnail compositions.

days.title: Drawing
days.work: Draw the strongest composition lightly with accurate proportion and overlap.

days.title: Shading
days.work: Shade the still life fully with a range of values.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Analyze a Dutch still life (e.g., Claesz) and compare its composition to yours.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write a 150-word artist statement explaining your choices.

weeks.assessment: Still life drawing and artist statement (rubric).

materials: tempera or acrylic paint (red, yellow, blue, white, black)

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Mix and paint a 12-part color wheel from primaries only.

days.title: Tints and shades
days.work: Paint tint and shade scales for two colors.

days.title: Color schemes
days.work: Paint four small squares showing complementary, analogous, monochromatic and triadic schemes.

days.title: Neutrals
days.work: Mix browns and grays by combining complements.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Label your swatches and quiz yourself on color vocabulary.

materials: images of Van Gogh and Picasso Blue Period works

days.title: Analyze mood
days.work: Compare Van Gogh's 'Starry Night' and Picasso's 'The Old Guitarist' and describe how color creates mood.

days.title: Same scene, two moods
days.work: Paint the same simple landscape twice, once warm and once cool.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose a personal place and sketch three thumbnails for a landscape painting.

days.title: Set criteria
days.work: Write criteria for the painting (color scheme, focal point, depth).

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Discuss which thumbnail best meets the criteria and why.

days.title: Underpainting
days.work: Block in background, middle ground and foreground with a thin underpainting.

days.title: Background
days.work: Paint the sky and distant areas lighter and cooler for atmospheric perspective.

days.title: Middle ground
days.work: Paint the middle ground with more detail and saturation.

days.title: Foreground
days.work: Paint the foreground with the most detail and contrast.

days.title: Details
days.work: Add final details and sign the painting.

objectives: Critique with personal vs. established criteria

days.title: Feldman critique
days.work: Use the describe-analyze-interpret-judge method to critique a famous landscape.

days.title: Self-critique
days.work: Critique your own painting with both personal and established criteria and note differences.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Make one revision to strengthen the focal point.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write an artist statement for the painting.

days.title: Mini show
days.work: Display drawings and painting for family and explain one choice in each.

objectives: Read rhythms with whole through sixteenth notes

days.title: Note values
days.work: Complete musictheory.net lessons on note and rest durations and clap 8 rhythms.

days.title: Time signatures
days.work: Identify meter in 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 excerpts and conduct each pattern.

days.title: Sixteenth notes
days.work: Count and clap sixteenth-note rhythms with 1-e-and-a syllables.

days.title: Bucket drumming
days.work: Perform a 16-bar bucket drumming rhythm with a metronome.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a rhythm-reading quiz on musictheory.net exercises.

objectives: Read notes on treble and bass clef

days.title: Treble clef
days.work: Learn treble clef note names and complete a note-naming drill.

days.title: Bass clef
days.work: Learn bass clef note names and complete a drill.

days.title: Keyboard
days.work: Locate notes on a keyboard and play C, G and F major scales.

days.title: Steps
days.work: Build major scales using the whole-whole-half pattern.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a note-reading and scale quiz.

materials: recordings of Hildegard von Bingen, a troubadour song, Palestrina and a madrigal

days.title: Chant
days.work: Listen to Gregorian chant and Hildegard von Bingen and describe texture and melody.

days.title: Polyphony
days.work: Listen to a Palestrina mass movement and identify the interweaving voices.

days.title: Secular music
days.work: Listen to a troubadour song and an English madrigal and compare to sacred music.

days.title: Global connections
days.work: Listen to Japanese gagaku and West African kora music and compare to European music of the same era.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a listening log comparing three pieces using musical vocabulary.

objectives: Identify forms (AB, ABA, rondo, theme and variations)
materials: recordings of Mozart 'Twinkle' variations, Beethoven 'Für Elise'

days.title: Dynamics and tempo
days.work: Learn Italian dynamic and tempo terms and mark them while listening to a piece.

days.title: Rondo
days.work: Map the form of 'Für Elise' (ABACA) with colored blocks.

days.title: Variations
days.work: Listen to Mozart's 'Twelve Variations on Ah vous dirai-je, Maman' and describe how each variation changes.

days.title: Interpretation
days.work: Compare two performances of the same piece and explain how performers' choices change expression.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a form and expression quiz.

days.title: Triads
days.work: Build C, F and G major triads on keyboard or ukulele.

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: Physical Education 7
courses.description: Seventh-grade physical education emphasizing team-building, invasion and net games, striking and fielding, dance, track and field, and outdoor pursuits, all tied to personal fitness. Students take the FITNESSGRAM (California's grade 7 Physical Fitness Test), set SMART goals, learn the FITT principle and heart-rate training zones, and finish the year with a self-designed fitness plan. Most sessions include a dynamic warm-up, skill practice, game play and cool-down; they can be done in a yard, park or community center with siblings, parents or a homeschool group.
courses.framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards (Grade 7); 2009 CA Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-7.1.1: Combine manipulative, locomotor and nonlocomotor skills into movement patterns in individual, dual and team activities.
standards.PE-7.1.2: Demonstrate mature techniques for throwing, catching, striking and kicking in modified game situations.
standards.PE-7.1.3: Demonstrate offensive and defensive skills (passing, dribbling, guarding, marking) in invasion and net games.
standards.PE-7.1.4: Perform rhythmic and dance sequences with a partner or group, including line and cultural dances.
standards.PE-7.1.5: Demonstrate basic skills of an individual or outdoor activity (orienteering, jump rope, track and field events).
standards.PE-7.2.1: Explain and apply offensive and defensive strategies in invasion, net/wall and striking/fielding games.
standards.PE-7.2.2: Analyze movement performance using biomechanical principles such as force, follow-through and base of support.
standards.PE-7.2.3: Explain how to create space and use teamwork to achieve a goal in game play.
standards.PE-7.3.1: Participate in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity a minimum of four days each week.
standards.PE-7.3.2: Assess muscular strength, muscular endurance, aerobic capacity, flexibility and body composition using a fitness assessment.
standards.PE-7.3.3: Meet age- and gender-specific fitness standards (Healthy Fitness Zone) for aerobic capacity, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility and body composition.
standards.PE-7.3.4: Develop and implement a one-week personal physical fitness plan using the FITT principle.
standards.PE-7.4.1: Explain the FITT principle (frequency, intensity, time, type) and the principles of overload, specificity and progression.
standards.PE-7.4.2: Identify and calculate target heart-rate zones and monitor intensity during activity.
standards.PE-7.4.3: Explain the components of a proper warm-up and cool-down and how they prevent injury.
standards.PE-7.5.1: Demonstrate responsible personal and social behavior, including safety, fair play and sportsmanship.
standards.PE-7.5.2: Accept responsibility for individual improvement and set SMART goals.
standards.PE-7.5.3: Work cooperatively with group members to solve problems and accomplish goals; demonstrate leadership.

courses.subject: HEALTH
courses.title: Health Education 7
courses.description: A skills-based health course for early adolescence covering nutrition and physical activity, mental, emotional and social health, injury prevention and safety (including online safety), alcohol, tobacco/vaping and other drugs, growth and development, and personal and community health. Each unit pairs essential concepts with the eight CA health skills—analyzing influences, accessing valid information, communication, decision making, goal setting, practicing healthy behaviors and advocacy. Sensitive topics in the growth and development unit are designed for parent-led discussion consistent with family values.
courses.framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grades 7–8); 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-7.1.1.N: Identify the six major nutrients and their functions; describe how to use MyPlate and nutrition labels.
standards.H-7.1.4.N: Describe the benefits of and barriers to physical activity and healthy eating, including the relationship among diet, activity and healthy weight.
standards.H-7.2.1.N: Analyze internal and external influences (media, culture, peers, advertising) on food choices and physical activity.
standards.H-7.3.1.N: Access and evaluate valid nutrition information, including identifying fad diets and false claims.
standards.H-7.6.1.N: Set a personal goal to improve dietary practices and physical activity and track progress.
standards.H-7.7.1.N: Practice healthy eating, including planning balanced meals and snacks and proper food safety.
standards.H-7.1.1.M: Describe characteristics of mental and emotional health and the relationship among stress, emotions and physical health.
standards.H-7.1.3.M: Identify signs of depression, anxiety and suicide risk and describe ways to get help from trusted adults.
standards.H-7.1.6.M: Describe characteristics of healthy and unhealthy relationships, including bullying and cyberbullying.
standards.H-7.4.1.M: Use effective verbal and nonverbal communication, active listening and I-messages to resolve conflicts.
standards.H-7.5.1.M: Use a decision-making process to address social and emotional situations.
standards.H-7.7.1.M: Practice healthy strategies to manage stress, anger and difficult emotions.
standards.H-7.8.1.M: Encourage others to seek help and promote a positive, inclusive school and community climate.
standards.H-7.1.2.S: Explain the causes of common injuries and ways to prevent them at home, outdoors and in sports.
standards.H-7.1.5.S: Describe safe and responsible use of the internet and social media, including privacy and dealing with online predators.
standards.H-7.1.7.S: Describe emergency preparedness for earthquakes, wildfires and other disasters in California.
standards.H-7.5.1.S: Use a decision-making process to evaluate risky situations, including violence, weapons and gang involvement.
standards.H-7.7.1.S: Demonstrate basic first aid and how to respond to emergencies, including calling 911.
standards.H-7.1.1.A: Describe the short- and long-term effects of alcohol, tobacco, e-cigarettes, cannabis and other drugs on the body and brain.
standards.H-7.1.3.A: Explain the addictive nature of nicotine and other substances and the process of dependency.
standards.H-7.1.6.A: Describe safe use and storage of prescription and over-the-counter medicines, including risks of misuse such as fentanyl-laced pills.
standards.H-7.2.1.A: Analyze how marketing, media, peers and family influence decisions about alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-7.4.2.A: Demonstrate refusal skills to avoid alcohol, tobacco, vaping and drug use.
standards.H-7.8.1.A: Advocate for a tobacco- and drug-free lifestyle and community.
standards.H-7.1.1.G: Describe physical, social, mental and emotional changes during adolescence and puberty.
standards.H-7.1.4.G: Explain the structure and function of the reproductive systems and the role of hormones (parent-led).
standards.H-7.1.7.G: Describe the importance of sleep, hygiene and personal responsibility for health during adolescence.
standards.H-7.3.1.G: Identify trusted adults and valid resources for questions about growth and development.
standards.H-7.4.1.G: Demonstrate communication skills to set personal boundaries and respect the boundaries of others.
standards.H-7.1.1.P: Explain how communicable and noncommunicable diseases are caused, transmitted and prevented.
standards.H-7.1.3.P: Describe the importance of regular medical and dental checkups, vaccinations and health screenings.
standards.H-7.1.6.P: Explain how environmental factors such as air and water quality affect personal and community health.
standards.H-7.3.1.P: Access valid health information and health services in the community.
standards.H-7.8.1.P: Advocate for a personal, family or community health issue such as clean air, recycling or disease prevention.
